title: Services Overview
meta_description: Consulting and delivery across eight deep-tech expertise domains, run as one governed delivery system with shared platforms and named gates.

blocks.x: Eight expertise domains, 54 engineering practices, one governed delivery system. Whichever domain you enter, the contract is identical: a business metric signed before delivery starts, an architecture you can interrogate before kickoff, releases that clear gates whose evidence is named in advance, and a handover your own team can run on a bad day.
How the eight domains divide the work
blocks.sub: The seams where enterprises actually buy — decision, action, platform, trust and compute, with the metric each domain is managed on

blocks.x: The map is cut along the seams where enterprises actually buy: what carries the decision (Applied AI), what acts on it (Agentic AI), what feeds the decision (Data & Lakehouse), what protects it (Cybersecurity), what runs the estate (Cloud & Platform), what reaches past classical limits (Quantum & Advanced Compute), what makes records verifiable (Blockchain & Digital Trust), and what connects the decision to physical operations (IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics). Practices inside a domain share tooling, hiring bar and standards; the domains share one gate model and one evidence format.

blocks.x: Where our sector depth sits — and how to read it
blocks.sub: Published structure, not claims: sub-industry capability pages per domain × industry, countable and verifiable

blocks.x: Depth is not a claim, it is a published structure: for every domain × industry cell below, the number is the count of sub-industry capability pages live on this site — each one a written sector brief with workflows, controls and a first-month plan. Where a cell is light, the domain-level sector brief covers the ground; where it is dark, you can descend to named sub-industries today.

blocks.x: The engagement ladder — four rungs, no leaps of faith
blocks.sub: Diagnostic, provability sprint, delivery slice, industrialization — enter at the rung your evidence supports

blocks.x: Work enters at the rung that matches the evidence you already hold. The ladder is deliberately short: the provability sprint exists so that nobody buys a large program on a hypothesis, and the diagnostic exists so the first build starts from a baseline your CFO and your auditors both accept.

blocks.x: The operating contract behind every service page
blocks.sub: Signed baseline, named gates, patent-mapped methods — the clauses that hold across all eight domains

blocks.x: Three clauses hold across all eight domains and every practice inside them. First, the baseline is signed by the metric owner before the build starts — no metric, no build. Second, releases clear gates whose evidence is named in advance, so a blocked release is a process working, not a crisis. Third, the handover includes the runbook, the eval suite and the operating console: the capability to run the system, not just the code that happens to be deployed today.

Where our patent-pending method families strengthen a gate, the service page names them and maps each family to the gate it reinforces — you can read the capability summary on the method map without asking for a briefing first.

Start with the two-week diagnostic — it ends with a signed baseline and a scored gate map for your estate, whichever domain you land in. Bring the metric you own; we will tell you honestly which gates you would fail today.
